Both these appeals arise out of common judgment and award passed in MVC Nos.2335 and 2336 of 2017 by the X Additional District and Sessions Judge and Member Addl. MACT, Belagavi dated 11.01.2019 claiming for enhancement of the compensation.
2. We refer the parties as per their rank before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.

3. It was the case of appellants/petitioners before the Tribunal that on 09.07.2010 at about 10.30 p.m. son of petitioner in MVC No.2335/2017 by name Santosh Yellappa Mushangol and son of petitioner Nos.1 and 2 in MVC No.2336/2017 by name Bharatkumar Muddas were going in a motorcycle bearing No.KA-65/H-4548 on Solapur-Ratnagiri National Highway.
Deceased Santosh was riding the motorcycle and Bharatkumar was pillion rider.
At about 10.30 p.m.
Both the riders of the motorcycle reached near Alkod M village and they met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing No.MP-09/HG-5612 by its driver.
As a result of which, both the riders of the motorcycle sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the spot.
Respondent No.1 was owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2 was insurer of the lorry at the relevant point of time.

4. It is the contention of the petitioners in MVC No.2335/2017 that deceased Bharatkumar was aged about 21 years at the time of accident and was serving in West Coast Paper Mill at Dandeli and earning salary of Rs.20,000/- p.m. and was maintaining the family.
Petitioners were depending upon his earnings.
With these reasons petitioners had claimed compensation of Rs.65,00,000/-.
5. Petitioners in MVC No.2335/2017 have also impleaded owner of the motorcycle i.e., legal heirs of deceased Santosh as respondent Nos.3(A-C) before the Tribunal.

6. It was the contention of the petitioners in MVC No.2336/2017 that deceased Santosh was aged about 21 years at the time of the accident and he was also serving in West Coast Paper Mill at Dandeli and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Petitioners were depending upon the earnings of the deceased.

With these reasons petitioners had claimed Rs.65,00,000/- as compensation.
7.
Respondent No.2 is insurer has filed written statement in both the petitions and contentions are more or less similar.

It has denied all the averments stated in the petitions and has contended that rider of the motorcycle as well as driver of the lorry had no valid driving licence to drive respective Smt.Mariyamma W/O Balanarshimalu vs Mr.Pavankumar Sharma S/O Mohanlal on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164565713/
4 vehicle at the time of the alleged accident.

sentences.text: Liability of respondent No.2 in both the petitions are restricted to terms and conditions of policy of insurance and holding of valid and effective driving licence by the driver of the lorry.
With these reasons, he prayed for dismissal of the petitions.
8. Tribunal had framed relevant issues on the basis of pleadings in both the cases.
9. The Tribunal clubbed both the matters and recorded common evidence.
10. The petitioners in both the cases to prove their contentions have examined P.Ws.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P15.
Respondent No.2 has not led any evidence.

11. The Tribunal appreciating pleadings and evidence on record vide impugned judgment and award dated 11.01.2019 awarded compensation of Rs.12,39,600/- in MVC No.2335/2017 under different heads, which are as under.

Sl. No. Heads Amount (Rs.)

Sl. No. Heads Amount (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 12,09,600  2. Loss of estate 15,000  3. Funeral expenses 15,000
13. Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioners in both the petitions have filed these appeals seeking for the enhancement of the compensation.
14. We have heard the arguments of the learned counsel for both the sides and perused the records.

Following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of the compensation as sought in the appeal?
ii) What Order?
16. The Tribunal on appreciation of the pleadings and evidence held that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry by its driver bearing No.MP- 09/HG-5612.
This finding is not challenged by respondent Nos.1 and 2 by filing the appeal or cross objection.
Therefore, there is no need for reconsidering the said finding.

17. Learned counsel for the appellants in both the cases has vehemently contended that Tribunal has not taken into account of Exs.P7 and 9 about the salary of the deceased as Rs.20,000/- in both the cases and taken notional income as Rs.8,000/- p.m.

He has further contended that in case if salary certificates were not proved by the appellants, then the Tribunal ought to have taken notional income of the deceased on the basis of income determined in the schedule of Lok Adalath i.e.,
Rs.10,250/- p.m.
In view of non-consideration of the same, injustice is caused to the appellants and just and fair amount of compensation is not awarded to them.
He further contended that amount of compensation awarded under different heads are also meager.
Therefore, prayed to enhance the amount of compensation.
18. Learned counsel for respondent No.2-insurer supports the impugned judgment and contends that there is no need to interfere in the said finding.

19. MFA No.101910/2019 arises of MVC No2335/2017, the Tribunal has taken age of the deceased as 24 years on the - 10 - basis of Ex.P6 and notional income of the deceased as Rs.8,000/- p.m. and added 40% as future prospects and deducted 50% towards personal expenses and awarded the compensation.
Age of the deceased and multiplier applied by the Tribunal are not disputed.

Therefore, the age of the deceased is taken as 24 years and suitable multiplier applicable is '18'.
20.
The main contention of the learned counsel for the appellants is that income of the deceased was not properly considered.
Let us consider the same.

The Tribunal has rightly rejected Ex.P7 on the ground that author of the said document was not examined and he was not a permanent employee in the West Coast Paper Mills at Dandeli and hence, it does not call for any interference.
The Tribunal on the basis of guess work taken notional income as Rs.8,000/- p.m.

As rightly submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants, in the schedule of income prepared by the Lok Adalath to settle the disputes, the income of the person who has failed to prove his income, the notional income is taken as Rs.10,250/- for the accident that had taken place during 2010.

23. MFA No.101911/2019 arises out of MVC No.2336/2017.
Age of the deceased was taken as 22 years on the basis of Ex.P8 and his income was taken as Rs.8,000/- p.m. and multiplier as '18'.
There is no dispute regarding age of the deceased as well as multiplier accepted by the Tribunal.
The dispute is in respect of income of the deceased.
The main contention of the learned counsel for the appellants is that income of the deceased was not properly considered.
Let us consider the same.

The Tribunal has rightly rejected Ex.P7 on - 13 - the ground that author of the said document was not examined and he was not a permanent employee in the West Coast Paper Mills at Dandeli and it does not call for any interference.

Smt.Mariyamma W/O Balanarshimalu vs Mr.Pavankumar Sharma S/O Mohanlal on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164565713/
7 24.
The Tribunal on the basis of guess work has taken notional income as Rs.8,000/- p.m.

As rightly submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants, in the schedule of income prepared by the Lok Adalath, to settle the disputes, the income of the person who has failed to prove his income, the notional income is taken as Rs.10,250/- for the accident that had taken place during 2010.
The Tribunal ought to have taken the said income as income of the deceased for assessment of the compensation.
In view of the same, it calls for interference and income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,250/- p.m.
40% of the income has to be added to the income assessed by this court towards future prospects.
Deceased was unmarried.
Therefore, 50% of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
On the basis of said calculation, the compensation to be awarded under the head loss of dependency is Rs.7,125/- x 12 x 18 = Rs.15,49,800/-.
In this case, there were four dependents to the deceased, i.e., his parents, brother and sister.
Out of them, brother and sister are not entitled for compensation under the head loss of consortium and parents are only entitled for compensation under the said head.

As per the law laid down in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), Magma General Insurance Company (supra) and N.Jayashree (supra),
Rs.44,000/- each is to be awarded towards loss of consortium and Rs.16,500/- each is to be awarded towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Thus, petitioners are entitled for following compensation:
 Sl. No. Heads Amount (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 15,49,800  2. Loss of consortium 88,000
3 . Loss of estate 16,500
4. Funeral expenses 16,500  Total 16,70,800 26.

In all, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.16,70,800/- as against Rs.12,39,600/- awarded by the Tribunal i.e., claimants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.4,31,200/-.
- 15 - 27.
It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was owner and respondent No.2 was insurer of the said vehicle and policy of insurance was in force as on the date of the accident.
Therefore, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are liable to pay the said amount of compensation.
28. For the above said discussions, we answer point No.1 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER The appeals in MFA Nos.101910 and 101911 of 2019 are partly allowed with costs.

The appellants in MFA No.101911/2019 are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,70,800/- as against Rs.12,39,600/-
- 16 - awarded by the Tribunal i.e., they are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,31,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till payment of the entire amount of compensation.
Respondent No.2 insurer shall deposit the said enhanced amount of compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
The remaining part of the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is kept intact.

The appellants in MFA No.101910/2019 are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,26,800/- as against Rs.12,39,600/- awarded by the Tribunal i.e., they are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.3,87,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till payment of the entire amount of compensation.
The appellants in MFA No.101911/2019 are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,70,800/- as against Rs.12,39,600/-
- 16 - awarded by the Tribunal i.e., they are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,31,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till payment of the entire amount of compensation.
Respondent No.2 insurer shall deposit the said enhanced amount of compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
The remaining part of the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is kept intact.

In view of the same, it calls for interference and income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,250/- p.m.
40% of the income has to be added to the income assessed by this court towards future prospects.
Deceased was unmarried.

Out of them, brother and sister are not entitled for compensation under the head loss of consortium and parents are only entitled for compensation under the said head.

 Sl. No. Heads Amount (Rs.)
